Hi Stephanie,

We signed up last week (org: Frostbyte Labs) and were immediately excited to try Redwood for a prototype. We completed the quick onboarding but only consumed ~3k tokens so far — we're still wiring model prompts into our pipeline and hit a few configuration snags.

Would it be possible to get a small self-serve top-up or a 14-day extension on the welcome credits so our engineers can validate model selection and latency under real traffic? If there's a standard PLG welcome-boost process, happy to follow it — we just want to avoid hitting the wall while we test.

A few quick notes:

- Current blockers: embedding latency spike on larger batches; 429s when we burst test

Thanks,
Elena

Hi Elena — welcome, and great to meet you. I approved a self-serve welcome boost for Frostbyte Labs: $2,000 of platform credits have been added to your account and will show up in the billing dashboard within a few minutes.

What I did:
- Issued $2,000 trial credits (immediate, no PO required)
- Attached the short trial terms we use for boosts (trial-terms-v2.pdf)
- Sent a DocuSign link for an optional AUP acknowledgement if your procurement team needs it: https://docusign.com/embedded?envelopeId=abc123

Next steps I recommend to get you unblocked quickly:
1) Try the streaming embedding flow with batch size=32 and enable the experimental KV cache (reduced latency for repeated contexts).
2) For reranking, pin the model to a 2k context variant to lower token costs while you validate.
3) If you still see 429s on bursts, reply with a short log snippet and we can spin up a small dedicated burst lane temporarily.

If you'd like, we can do a 20-minute call this week to walk your engineer through the SDK patterns that tend to help here. I’m copying Avery (Sales Ops) so we can track the boost on our side.

Cheers,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Quick check-in — tips to get the most from the boost

Hi Elena — checking in quickly since the boost went into your account last Friday. I noticed low token consumption so far and wanted to share a few high-impact tips that typically shorten time-to-value:

- Start with single-shot embeddings (batch=16) to validate semantic similarity, then increase batch size when you’re comfortable.
- Use the cheapest compatible model for embedding experiments (we recommend redwood-embed-1-small for quick iteration).
- Enable prefix caching for reranking pipelines — it can cut token spend by up to 40% on repeated contexts.

If useful, I can hop on a 20-minute screen share with your ML engineer to walk through the exact request patterns. Here are a couple of quick windows that work for me this week: 2027-04-07 09:30 or 2027-04-08 11:00 PT — pick one and I’ll send an invite.

If you’re hitting 429s, please forward a short log excerpt and I’ll engage infra to add a temporary burst lane.

Best,
Stephanie
